title: Forensic log-lineage readiness cheat sheet: RBACv2 + SIEM export for SOC 2 / ISO 27001
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, auditor-facing readiness cheat sheet focused on log lineage, retention, and curated evidence for RBACv2 events and SIEM exports in support of SOC 2 and ISO 27001 reviews. Used by security, SRE, and platform teams to assemble minimally-sufficient artifacts quickly.

Audience:
- Audit leads and technical owners prepping evidence
- SRE / Platform engineers responsible for SIEM export and retention
- Security reviewers mapping RBAC events to control objectives

Scope:
- RBAC v2: role changes, permission grant/revoke, policy rollouts, service-account activity
- Audit log schema and canonical field set exported to SIEM (Elastic / Splunk / BigQuery snapshots)
- Evidence automation: snapshotting, hashing, secure delivery, and lineage proof
- Control mapping for SOC 2 (common criteria) and ISO 27001 (A.9, A.12) that rely on auditability

Quick-read summary (one-liner):
Ensure every RBAC change is captured with: who, when, object, before_state, after_state, reason/ticket, request_id/trace_id; export those fields to a hardened SIEM index with immutable retention snapshots and SHA256ed evidence bundles for auditor delivery.

Canonical audit log fields (flattened list - required):
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC
- event_type: rbac.role.assign | rbac.role.revoke | rbac.policy.update | auth.token.create | auth.token.revoke
- actor_id: {user_id | service_account_id}
- actor_email: user@redwood.ai (when available)
- target_id: role|resource identifier
- target_type: role | resource | permission
- before: JSON string (nullable)
- after: JSON string (nullable)
- reason: free-text or ticket id
- trace_id: correlation id linking to request/trace
- request_id: infra request id (if different)
- source: service name (iam-service, console-api, admin-cli)
- ip_address: client IP (if applicable)
- retention_tag: e.g., "evidence.bound:365d"
- event_hash: sha256 of the canonical flattened event payload (for lineage)

Minimum export policy to SIEM (practical):
1) Map canonical fields above to SIEM index fields exactly (no nested blobs).
2) Export frequency: near-real-time (stream); fallback: hourly bulk export for missed windows.
3) Immutable snapshots: daily index snapshot with retention policy >= 365 days (SOC 2 typical) or as required by legal/regional rules.
4) Retention layering: hot (30d), warm (30-90d), cold/archive (>=365d) - ensure archived copies are write-once where supported.

Sample SIEM queries (examples auditors like to see)
- Splunk (SPL):
  index=rbac_audit sourcetype=rbac:event event_type=rbac.role.assign | table _time, actor_email, target_id, reason, trace_id
- Elastic KQL:
  index:rbac_audit AND event_type: "rbac.role.revoke" | columns timestamp, actor_id, before, after, trace_id
- BigQuery SQL (daily snapshot table):
  SELECT timestamp, actor_email, event_type, target_type, request_id FROM `redwood-prod.rbac_audit.daily_snapshot` WHERE DATE(timestamp)=DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 1 DAY) LIMIT 100

Evidence curation flow (automated playbook):
1) Trigger: audit request or running quarterly evidence collection job.
2) Create query spec (saved SIEM query id) that produces canonical flattened rows for requested period/control.
3) Export rows to GCS/S3 staging bucket under /audit_delivery/{control}/{YYYY-MM-DD}/raw.csv
4) Generate canonical manifest (manifest.csv) with: filename, row_count, sha256 (of raw.csv), start_ts, end_ts, query_id, generated_by
5) Produce compressed archive: tar -czf {control}_{date}.tar.gz raw.csv manifest.csv metadata.txt
6) Compute archive checksum: sha256sum {archive} > {archive}.sha256
7) Encrypt archive with customer-facing KMS key and upload to hardened artifact bucket with restricted ACLs
8) Record delivery in evidence log: evidence_id, control, archive_path, checksum, generated_by, generated_at, retention_until
9) (Optional) Publish pre-signed URL to auditor with one-time password and notify via secure channel.

Automated job example (cron)
- cron: 0 3 * * * /usr/local/bin/generate-audit-bundle --control RBAC-CHANGE-LOG --days 7 --out /audit_delivery/rbac/$(date +\"%F\")
- generate-audit-bundle pseudo steps: query SIEM -> write CSV -> manifest -> tar.gz -> checksum -> kms-encrypt -> upload -> record to DB

Proof of lineage (what auditors accept):
- event_hash on each event (sha256 of canonical flattened JSON) stored in SIEM record
- archive checksum (sha256) + manifest includes per-file hashes
- signed manifest (PGP or KMS-signed metadata) for tamper evidence
- correlation to trace_id/request_id that links to application traces (provide span ids or trace logs as needed)
- retention policy policies and configuration screenshots (console) showing index lifecycle rules

Control mapping examples (short form):
- SOC 2 CC6.1 (Change control / logical access):
  Evidence: RBAC audit index export, role assignment events, change ticket references captured in 'reason' field.
  Notes: Provide snapshot for sample period, query showing a role grant + matching ticket in JIRA.

- ISO 27001 A.9.2 (User access management):
  Evidence: user provisioning/revocation events, service-account lifecycle logs, proof of periodic review (scheduling job logs).
  Notes: Show suppression windows where service accounts auto-rotate; include playbook for emergency access revocation.

Gap analysis checklist (quick triage):
- [ ] Are before/after states recorded for policy updates? (gap -> develop serializer & include in 'before'/'after')
- [ ] Are ticket references auto-populated into reason field? (gap -> enrich lambda that writes event)
- [ ] Is event_hash computed consistently? (gap -> reconcile hashing library across services)
- [ ] Is trace_id included on all events? (gap -> instrument entrypoints to attach trace)
- [ ] Export mapping present in SIEM runbook? (gap -> update runbook and add unit test)
- [ ] Is evidence snapshot automation running and monitored? (gap -> add alert if job fails >2 runs)

Remediation playbook template (per-gap):
- Issue: missing ticket id in 'reason' for console-initiated grants.
  Action: update console-api to inject 'reason' by prompting user for ticket or defaulting to 'manual-admin' with required justification field.
  Owner: Eli Rivera
  ETA: 2026-01-15
  Validation: add automated SIEM query that measures percent of events with non-null reason (target >95%)

Deliverable checklist for auditors (what to hand over):
- Exported SIEM query (saved query ID) + sample query results (CSV) covering request window
- Archive bundle (tar.gz) with manifest and archive.sha256 (encrypted and/or signed)
- Screenshot of SIEM index ILM (index lifecycle management) settings showing retention tiers
- System config snippet showing where event_hash is computed (code link + commit hash)
- Sample event JSON (3 examples: role.assign, role.revoke, policy.update) and mapping doc explaining fields
- Evidence log entry (proof of upload + delivery record with presigned URL expiry)

Anticipated auditor Q&A (short answers):
- Q: How do you ensure logs are not tampered after creation?
  A: Events include event_hash and are indexed into an append-only SIEM index. Daily archive snapshots are checksumed and stored in a write-once cold tier; manifests are KMS-signed.

- Q: Can you show a granular example linking a role grant to a JIRA ticket and a trace?
  A: Yes — provide sample CSV row: timestamp,actor_email,event_type,reason(jira-1234),trace_id=req-abc-123. Provide Splunk query and matching APM trace link for the trace_id.

- Q: What if an event was missed because of a downstream outage?
  A: We have hourly bulk exports as a fallback. The evidence manifest includes 'export_method' (stream|bulk) and 'bulk_export_backfill' entries. We also run an audit job that compares expected counts per service against actual indexed counts and raises alerts.

- Q: How long is evidence retained and who approves deletion?
  A: Default retention for RBAC audit index is 365 days. Archive retention is 7 years for customers with long-term retention requirements. Deletions must be approved by the InfoSec manager and recorded in the evidence log with justification and approver name.

Sample small-size event examples (plain rows):
- 2026-02-01T14:03:12Z | rbac.role.assign | actor_email=maya.patel@redwood.ai | target_id=role:read-only | before=null | after={\"permissions\": [\"read:logs\"]} | reason=JIRA-SEC-421 | trace_id=trace-11b2
- 2026-02-03T09:22:03Z | rbac.policy.update | actor_id=svc-deploy-01 | before={\"rules\":...} | after={\"rules\":...} | reason=auto-rollout | event_hash=sha256:abc...

Appendix: validation commands and small scripts
- Verify archive checksum: sha256sum -c {archive}.sha256
- Verify per-row hashes: python3 verify_hashes.py --input raw.csv --hash-field event_hash
- Generate signed manifest (KMS-marked): gcloud kms asymmetric-sign --key=projects/.../cryptoKeys/evidence-key --digest-file=manifest.sha256 --signature-file=manifest.sig

Next steps (actionable short list):
1) Run the gap checklist and assign owners to each unchecked item (owner + ETA).
2) Add two saved SIEM queries (one for role.assign, one for policy.update) and link them to evidence jobs.
3) Create a runbook for auditors describing delivery and the verifier commands (sha256, manifest verification).
4) Schedule a dry-run delivery to internal audit one week before the external audit date.

Notes and references:
- Confluence: RBACv2 design page (linked in metadata)
- JIRA tickets referenced above for remediation work
- PR for SIEM mapping: linked_artifacts
